- Overestimate prices after recent spikes (especially when sentiment is negative or neutral) — reduce forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) — add 2–5% to forecast to compensate for downward pressure.
- Lagged corrections: if true outcome is higher than forecast 3–5 days ago, adjust next forecast downward by 1–3%.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Overshoot after bullish sentiment: if sentiment > 0.3 and forecast > 10% above prior 30d mean, cap at +5% deviation.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings — if sentiment flips sharply, delay adjustment until 2–3 days later unless price is clearly trending.
